commits.message:
Add the trusted-head authority child-process fixture the watcher journeys import

watcher-installed-journey.test.ts already imported
tests/support/trusted-head-process-fixture.js, but the fixture, its forked
entry module, and its own runtime test had not been committed, so a clean
checkout could not typecheck the watcher package. The fixture bundles the
current authority source with esbuild and forks it onto its own event loop,
the way the deployed sidecar runs.

Stop reading necessity artifacts from the scanner-confinement gate

The gate that confines `canonical_cbor_scan_v1` to its reviewed on-chain
consumers also parsed three Markdown necessity artifacts under
docs/exec-plans/evidence/necessity and failed whenever their pinned blueprint
identity drifted from the live build. Those documents are not test inputs:
the consumer set is now an explicit list in the test, and the on-chain
source scan, the complete-item staging checks, and the predicate negative
controls stay exactly as they were.

Restore the local full-pass entrypoint and make the test Postgres durable

The workspace typecheck was reproducibly red: midgard-node and
midgard-node-tools prefixed `tsc --noEmit` with builds of lucid-midgard and
midgard-sdk, and under `--workspace-concurrency=4` those two prebuild chains
raced on `tsup --clean` of the same midgard-core dist (ENOENT on unlink), which
aborted run-test-lanes-v1.mjs before any lane started. The prefix has been
dead since every package resolved its siblings from source through the
`midgard-source` export condition, so typecheck is now `tsc --noEmit` alone.

The prefix did have one live side effect: midgard-node's crash-probe child
processes and midgard-node-tools' `node --test` files run under plain node,
which resolves the workspace packages to `dist/`. That build now belongs to a
`pretest` in those two packages, which lane B runs serially, so there is a
single dist builder at a time and `pnpm test` works from a clean checkout.

scripts/start-test-postgres.sh starts the 127.0.0.1:5433 test server the node
suites need with the settings they assert (synchronous_commit=on server-wide,
no unix socket, 200 connections), initialising a persistent data directory on
first use and leaving any server already on the port untouched.

Integrate watcher persistence and current protocol work

Include all current contract, runtime, SDK, test, documentation, and tooling changes.

Watcher validation: local installed journey passed through proof, correction, and healthy successor; focused persistence and recovery checks passed. Three existing mixed replay fixture failures remain unchanged. Broader workspace validation is not asserted by this commit.
Keep validation resolver publications within the reserved size limit

Prove the installed validationTraceDispute watcher journeys

Cover the honest-response, operator-stall timeout, and cold-restart resume
lines through the production runner, refuse a forged move at its exact
check, and record the installation receipt.

Close the LOP and CEK context receipts against the rebuilt blueprint

Re-pin every ledger this wave touched to the fresh `aiken build --env testnet`
blueprint (sha256 7e478b66f681ed47d4bf63a9043641e7a1c47d02b9168ed71c183975cf9ed0e9,
compiler v1.1.23+5adf783), all with zero negative margins:

- CEK context: 2,927 entries, 24 distinct lifecycle shapes, worst execution
  3,541,587 mem / 1,645,575,835 cpu, worst signed transaction 15,108 bytes;
- CEK context publication: 36 entries, re-pinned from a pre-restructure
  `420a8327…` that was failing the live-blueprint check, worst signed
  publication 12,981 bytes;
- ScriptSources item maximum: 2,019 entries, worst execution 3,898,959 mem /
  1,854,545,673 cpu, worst signed transaction 15,108 bytes;
- ledger-output-proof publication: 34 entries, worst signed publication
  14,954 bytes.

The CEK context receipt records the stage-0 shared-item root cause — the
executor side, not the builder, was wrong — and confirms no semantic predicate
was weakened: `outer_fields_are_well_formed` already enforced the same
`mode == 0 || mode == 1` domain inside the canonical machine, and the
successor equality that carries the semantics is untouched.

The LOP receipt gains a §8 reconciliation: the three pre-existing
>15,000-byte validation-trace semantics re-measured across the whole 91-entry
resolver roster (two exceed the 15,872 signed-publication gate and are
escalated with numbers); the program doc §7 oversized checkpoint reconciled
against the fresh blueprint, where only three `availability_challenge` entries
remain above 16,384 and every oversized validation-dispute and
transition-trace body is gone; and a sweep of the fault-proof test surface for
raised transaction size, raised ExUnits, oversized publication and disabled
evaluation, with a disposition for each route.

Pin both polarities of the widened shared open-executor mode selector

`open_header` / `open_tail` now admit `mode_descriptor || mode_data`, which is
the full legal domain, so nothing in the previous fix pins that the selector
still refuses anything. Add the negative polarity at the exact clause: an
out-of-domain mode (2) is refused at both executors, with every other part of
each fixture the genuine canonical pair so the mode is the only thing that can
refuse. The selector is an `expect`, so its refusal traps rather than returning
`False` — hence `fail` tests.

This is coverage only; no predicate changed and the blueprint is byte-identical
at sha256 7e478b66f681ed47d4bf63a9043641e7a1c47d02b9168ed71c183975cf9ed0e9.
Full `aiken check --env testnet`: 4,014 tests, 4,014 passed, 0 failed.

Bring the resolve-inputs step dispatcher under the execution basis

The advance-integer positive measured 14,226,253 mem against the 13,200,000
basis; per-redeemer attribution put the dispatcher spend ~1.5M above its
ScriptSources sibling. Two sanctioned narrow-decode changes close it with no
semantic predicate change:

- decode the pending descriptor once and feed both carrier predicates
  (control_raw_is_bound_with_descriptor /
  control_raw_lop_is_pinned_with_descriptor; the old names remain as exact
  wrappers for the finalize dispatcher), saving ~1.07M mem;
- derive the successor work witness with splice_pending_successor_v1 (the
  membership-step plan's "successor by splice"), which replaces the two
  verified encoding tails instead of re-walking encode_control_raw and
  encode_pending; a fuzz test proves the splice byte-identical to the
  whole-record re-encode, and a tampered proof tail is refused.

The lifecycle now measures 13,100,448 mem / 4,378,032,009 cpu (99,552 mem
under basis); the dispatcher is 11,062 raw bytes. The advance-integer
positive is un-skipped with the standard basis assertion, leaving the
ledger-output-proof emulator suite at 20/20 with zero skips.

Accept both item modes in the shared open-header/open-tail executors

The CEK context binds descriptor-mode selection items into the shared
redeemer-item chain (cek-context-item-bind requires mode_descriptor at
context stage 0), but the open-header/open-tail executor semantics gated on
mode_data only, leaving every stage-0 shared item bindable yet unprovable.
Widen the two gates to the full step_v1 header/tail domain; the canonical
prevalidated_open_header/open_tail successor equality is unchanged and pins
the mode-dependent shape itself. invalid_header/invalid_tail deliberately
stay data-mode only. Both polarities covered for the descriptor mode.
Reconcile registry pins with the completed 54-category workflow roster

Record the mixed-width permutation receipt and re-pin the shared ledgers

The mixed-width mint ordering closure gains its measured receipt: selector
coverage at both the stage-8 mint item and the output value fold, the
producer proof-material pins, the registered 1,304-asset emulator
lifecycles in both polarities, and the measured envelope (worst execution
3,063,924 mem / 1,181,325,013 steps, worst signed transaction 15,108
bytes) against the fresh testnet blueprint. The ledger-output-proof
publication and ScriptSources item-max fit ledgers are regenerated against
that same blueprint. The consolidated CEK context lifecycle ledger keeps
its earlier pin: its regeneration is blocked by the pre-existing stage-0
shared item lifecycle red, which reproduces at the commit that installed
the stage graph and is independent of the permutation work.
Wire the validationTraceDispute runner into the watcher application registry

Install the validationTraceDispute production workflow surface and runner

The manifest-bound workflow admits only a freshly rebuilt validation-trace
challenge, binds every family reference script by manifest name, re-derives
the dispute cursor exclusively from live chain state on each invocation, and
journals a locally evaluated pre-submit intent before every transaction. The
admitted runner factory joins WORKFLOW_RUNNER_FACTORIES under the same
adapter surface as the other production families.
